Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's official GitHub repository using a tagged release archive over HTTPS. The `source` array entry points to a predictable tar.gz URL based on the version tag, which is a common and safe practice. The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, so the source integrity will be verified after download. There is no command substitution, no `pkgver()` function (so no dynamic version fetching), and no top-level code execution outside of standard variable assignments. The global scope consists only of declarative metadata and arrays, which are inert and cannot execute arbitrary commands. Therefore, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch and verify the source without executing any potentially malicious code.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No active code execution during source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build and packaging process for the vermouth application, which is a game and app launcher. The source is fetched from a legitimate upstream GitHub repository using a tagged release (v2.0.3), and the SHA-256 checksum matches the provided hash, ensuring integrity. The build process uses CMake with Ninja as the generator, which is common for KDE and Qt-based applications.

Dependencies are limited to well-known Qt6, Kirigami, and related libraries, all of which are reasonable for a Qt/KDE application. The package installs files into standard system locations under `$pkgdir`, and includes the license file in the expected directory. There are no suspicious commands such as `curl | bash`, `wget`, `eval`, or attempts to access sensitive files or network resources outside of the declared source.

The script does not perform any runtime modifications, obfuscated operations, or post-install actions beyond what is necessary for a typical desktop application. All operations align with standard AUR packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>

The source is fetched from the official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/dekomote/vermouth`) at a specific tagged release (`v2.0.3`), and the corresponding tarball is accompanied by a valid SHA-256 checksum: `e170f765554ea456a9761da97f19c7166022f577438dc5b3ae022761942c25f2`. This ensures integrity and reproducibility of the source.

All listed dependencies are typical for a Qt6/Kirigami-based desktop application on Linux, with no suspicious or out-of-scope packages. There are no scripts, commands, or executable content in this file—only declarative packaging data. The use of a pinned release tag (rather than a mutable branch) combined with a matching checksum indicates good supply-chain hygiene.

No evidence of obfuscation, unauthorized network activity, or malicious behavior is present. The file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and poses no security risk.
</details>
